source.text: ταύτας οὖν ἔχοντες τὰς ἐπαγγελίας, ἀγαπητοί, καθαρίσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ παντὸς μολυσμοῦ σαρκὸς καὶ πνεύματος, ἐπιτελοῦντες ἁγιωσύνην ἐν φόβῳ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: These therefore having the promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in [the] fear of God.

en.L: Therefore, having these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in [the] fear of God.
en.B: Dear friends, since these promises are ours, let us wash ourselves clean of every stain on body and spirit, and carry our holiness through to its goal as we live in the fear of God.
en.R: Dear friends, God has made these promises to us. So let us make ourselves clean from everything that makes our bodies or our spirits unclean. We have deep respect for God, so let us keep on growing until we are completely holy.

fr.L: Ayant donc ces promesses, bien-aimés, purifions-nous de toute souillure de la chair et de l’esprit, en menant la sainteté à son achèvement dans la crainte de Dieu.
fr.B: Chers amis, puisque ces promesses sont à nous, purifions-nous de toute souillure du corps et de l’esprit, et menons notre sainteté jusqu’à son but en vivant dans la crainte de Dieu.
fr.R: Chers amis, Dieu nous a fait ces promesses. Alors, rendons-nous purs : écartons tout ce qui salit notre corps ou notre esprit. Nous respectons profondément Dieu, alors continuons à grandir jusqu’à être complètement saints.

es.L: Así que, teniendo estas promesas, amados, purifiquémonos de toda contaminación de carne y de espíritu, perfeccionando la santidad en [el] temor de Dios.
es.B: Queridos amigos, ya que estas promesas son nuestras, limpiémonos de toda mancha del cuerpo y del espíritu, y llevemos nuestra santidad hasta su meta, viviendo en el temor de Dios.
es.R: Queridos amigos, Dios nos ha hecho estas promesas. Así que limpiémonos de todo lo que ensucia nuestro cuerpo o nuestro espíritu. Tenemos un profundo respeto por Dios, así que sigamos creciendo hasta ser completamente santos.

sw.L: Basi, wapendwa, kwa kuwa tuna ahadi hizi, na tujitakase na kila unajisi wa mwili na roho, tukiukamilisha utakatifu katika kumcha Mungu.
sw.B: Wapendwa, kwa kuwa ahadi hizi ni zetu, na tujisafishe na kila doa la mwili na la roho, tukiufikisha utakatifu wetu kwenye ukamilifu wake huku tukiishi katika kumcha Mungu.
sw.R: Wapendwa, Mungu ametupa ahadi hizi. Kwa hiyo na tujisafishe na kila kitu kinachoitia miili yetu au roho zetu unajisi. Tunamheshimu Mungu sana, kwa hiyo na tuendelee kukua mpaka tuwe watakatifu kabisa.

decisions.choice: these promises: the promises of God quoted in 6:16-18
decisions.reason: ταύτας ("these") points back to the Scripture promises Paul has just strung together in 6:16-18: God will live among his people, welcome them and be a Father to them. This verse closes that passage; the chapter break comes one verse too late.

decisions.choice: defilement of flesh and spirit: uncleanness of the whole person, outward and inward
alternatives: two kinds of sin, bodily sins and sins of the mind
flesh in the sense of a sinful nature
decisions.reason: μολυσμοῦ is a stain or pollution that makes something unclean for worship. Here σαρκὸς and πνεύματος together mean the whole person, the outward life and the inner self. The setting is 6:14-18, where the uncleanness is taking part in idol worship.

decisions.choice: perfecting holiness: carrying holiness through to its goal
decisions.reason: ἐπιτελοῦντες means to bring something to completion. The holiness believers already have as God's people is to be carried through in how they live.

decisions.choice: in the fear of God: in reverent awe of God
decisions.reason: "The fear of God" is the reverence and awe owed to God, as in 5:11 and Philippians 2:12. It is the setting in which holiness grows, not dread.

decisions.choice: beloved: those Paul loves, and whom God loves
alternatives: a polite form of address only
decisions.reason: ἀγαπητοί is a warm address. After the stern call of 6:14-18 Paul reminds the church that he speaks out of love.

decisions.choice: body (B); bodies (R)
decisions.reason: In this book Balanced and Readable usually turn "flesh" into "merely human". Here the word means the physical, outward side of a person paired with the spirit (m2), so Balanced and Readable say "body".

decisions.choice: dear friends
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 4:1, Balanced and Readable use a warm modern address in place of "beloved".

decisions.choice: God has made these promises to us
decisions.reason: Readable says who gave the promises (m1).

decisions.choice: la chair (L); le corps (B, R) (for chapters 7-11)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "la chair" wherever Paul says "flesh", as the style guide sets for sarx. Here the word is the outward, bodily side of a person set beside the spirit, so Balanced and Readable say "le corps", as the English says "body"; elsewhere in these chapters they give the sense ("selon des critères purement humains", 10:2-3; 11:18).

decisions.choice: amados (L); queridos amigos (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the other letters: Literal keeps "amados", and Balanced and Readable use the warm everyday address "queridos amigos", as the English does.

decisions.choice: wapendwa (every level)
decisions.reason: "Wapendwa" (beloved ones) is the ordinary Swahili address in a letter to people one loves, so it serves at every level where the English Balanced and Readable say "dear friends".

decisions.choice: unajisi
decisions.reason: "Unajisi" is ritual defilement, which follows on from "najisi" in 6:17; "uchafu" would be plain dirt.

source.text: Χωρήσατε ἡμᾶς· οὐδένα ἠδικήσαμεν, οὐδένα ἐφθείραμεν, οὐδένα ἐπλεονεκτήσαμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Make room for us; no one we wronged, no one we ruined, no one we took advantage of.

en.L: Make room for us: no one have we wronged, no one have we ruined, no one have we exploited.
en.B: Open your hearts to us. We have done no wrong to anyone, brought no one to ruin, and cheated no one.
en.R: Please open your hearts to us. We have not treated anyone unfairly. We have not ruined anyone. We have not cheated anyone.

fr.L: Faites-nous place : nous n’avons fait de tort à personne, nous n’avons ruiné personne, nous n’avons exploité personne.
fr.B: Ouvrez-nous votre cœur. Nous n’avons fait de tort à personne, nous n’avons causé la ruine de personne, nous n’avons dupé personne.
fr.R: S’il vous plaît, ouvrez-nous votre cœur. Nous n’avons été injustes envers personne. Nous n’avons ruiné la vie de personne. Nous n’avons trompé personne.

es.L: {{plural_you:Hágannos|Hacednos}} lugar: a nadie hemos agraviado, a nadie hemos arruinado, de nadie nos hemos aprovechado.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ábrannos|Abridnos}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón. No hemos hecho mal a nadie, no hemos llevado a nadie a la ruina, y no hemos engañado a nadie.
es.R: Por favor, {{plural_you:ábrannos|abridnos}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón. No hemos tratado injustamente a nadie. No hemos arruinado a nadie. No hemos engañado a nadie.

sw.L: Tupeni nafasi: hatukumdhulumu mtu yeyote, hatukumharibu mtu yeyote, hatukumnyonya mtu yeyote.
sw.B: Tufungulieni mioyo yenu. Hatujamtendea mtu yeyote vibaya, hatujamharibu mtu yeyote, wala hatujamdanganya mtu yeyote ili kujipatia faida.
sw.R: Tafadhali tufungulieni mioyo yenu. Hatujamtendea mtu yeyote isivyo haki. Hatujamharibu mtu yeyote. Hatujamdanganya mtu yeyote.

decisions.choice: make room for us: open your hearts to us
alternatives: make space for us in your homes
decisions.reason: Χωρήσατε means to make room for something. It picks up 6:11-13, where Paul says his heart is open wide to them and asks them to open theirs in return. After the warning of 6:14-7:1 he comes back to that appeal.

decisions.choice: three flat denials, perhaps answering charges made against Paul
alternatives: a general claim to good conduct
decisions.reason: οὐδένα ("no one") is put first three times for emphasis. Paul may be answering what some at Corinth said of him; 12:16-18 shows that he was suspected of taking advantage of them over money.

decisions.choice: ruined: brought to ruin, whether in faith and morals or in money
decisions.reason: ἐφθείραμεν can mean to corrupt or to ruin. Paul does not say in what way; he denies doing anyone harm of any kind.

decisions.choice: took advantage of: exploited someone for gain
decisions.reason: ἐπλεονεκτήσαμεν means to take more than one's share, to exploit. The same verb is used of Titus and Paul's other messengers in 12:17-18.

decisions.choice: Open your hearts to us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the room is to be made (m1).

decisions.choice: hatukumnyonya
decisions.reason: "Kunyonya" (to suck dry) is the everyday Swahili word for exploiting someone for gain, the sense of the meaning decision.

source.text: πρὸς κατάκρισιν οὐ λέγω, προείρηκα γὰρ ὅτι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν ἐστε εἰς τὸ συναποθανεῖν καὶ συζῆν.

records.literal_gloss: For condemnation not I speak, for I have said before that in the hearts of us you are, for the to die together and to live together.

en.L: I do not speak [this] for condemnation, for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
en.B: I am not saying this to condemn you. I have told you before: you are in our hearts, and we are bound to you in death and in life.
en.R: I am not saying this to blame you. I told you before that we love you deeply. Whether we die or live, we want to be with you.

fr.L: Je ne parle pas pour condamner, car j’ai déjà dit que vous êtes dans nos cœurs, pour mourir ensemble et pour vivre ensemble.
fr.B: Je ne dis pas cela pour vous condamner. Je vous l’ai déjà dit : vous êtes dans nos cœurs, et nous sommes liés à vous dans la mort comme dans la vie.
fr.R: Je ne dis pas cela pour vous faire des reproches. Je vous l’ai déjà dit : nous vous aimons profondément. Que nous mourions ou que nous vivions, nous voulons être avec vous.

es.L: No [lo] digo para condenación, porque he dicho antes que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en nuestros corazones, para morir juntos y para vivir juntos.
es.B: No digo esto para {{plural_you:condenarlos|condenaros}}. Ya {{plural_you:les|os}} he dicho antes: {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en nuestros corazones, y estamos unidos a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en la muerte y en la vida.
es.R: No digo esto para {{plural_you:culparlos|culparos}}. Ya {{plural_you:les|os}} dije antes que {{plural_you:los|os}} amamos profundamente. Sea que muramos o que vivamos, queremos estar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Sisemi [hivi] kwa kuwahukumu, kwa maana nimekwisha kusema kwamba mmo mioyoni mwetu, hata kufa pamoja na kuishi pamoja.
sw.B: Sisemi hivi ili kuwahukumu. Nimekwisha kuwaambia: mmo mioyoni mwetu, nasi tumefungamana nanyi katika kufa na katika kuishi.
sw.R: Sisemi hivi ili kuwalaumu. Niliwaambia zamani kwamba tunawapenda sana. Iwe tunakufa au tunaishi, tunataka kuwa pamoja nanyi.

decisions.choice: the denials of verse 2 do not accuse the church
decisions.reason: When Paul says he has wronged no one, it might sound as if he is accusing the Corinthians of wronging him. He says plainly that that is not his aim.

decisions.choice: said before: in 6:11-13, and perhaps in 3:2
decisions.reason: προείρηκα ("I have said before") most naturally points back within this letter, to 6:11-13, where Paul speaks of his heart opened wide to them (compare 3:2, "written on our hearts").

decisions.choice: to die together and to live together: a pledge of loyalty that nothing will break
alternatives: you are in our hearts so that you will die and live with us
decisions.reason: Friends in the Greek world spoke of being ready to die and live together. Paul puts dying first, perhaps because he faces death daily and lives by Christ's life (4:10-12). The Greek does not say who dies with whom; the sense is that Paul and the church belong together whatever happens.

decisions.choice: we are bound to you in death and in life
alternatives: you are in our hearts to die together and to live together
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the Greek infinitives into a clause that says what being in Paul's heart means (m3).

decisions.choice: we love you deeply
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "you are in our hearts" means.

source.text: πολλή μοι παρρησία πρὸς ὑμᾶς, πολλή μοι καύχησις ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν· πεπλήρωμαι τῇ παρακλήσει, ὑπερπερισσεύομαι τῇ χαρᾷ ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Great to me [is] boldness toward you, great to me boasting on behalf of you; I have been filled with the comfort, I overflow with the joy in all the affliction of us.

en.L: Great [is] my boldness toward you; great [is] my boasting about you. I have been filled with comfort; I am overflowing with joy in all our affliction.
en.B: I can speak to you very openly, and I have every reason to be proud of you. Comfort fills me, and joy floods over me in spite of all our hardship.
en.R: I speak to you openly and honestly, and I am very proud of you. I am full of comfort. Even with all our troubles, I have more joy than I can hold.

fr.L: Grande [est] ma franchise envers vous, grand [est] mon sujet de fierté à votre égard ; je suis rempli de réconfort, je déborde de joie dans toute notre détresse.
fr.B: Je peux vous parler en toute franchise, et j’ai toutes les raisons d’être fier de vous. Le réconfort me remplit, et la joie me submerge malgré toutes nos épreuves.
fr.R: Je vous parle ouvertement et honnêtement, et je suis très fier de vous. Je suis plein de réconfort. Malgré toutes nos difficultés, j’ai plus de joie que je ne peux en contenir.

es.L: Grande [es] mi franqueza con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; grande [es] mi motivo de gloria en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Estoy lleno de consuelo; sobreabundo de gozo en toda nuestra aflicción.
es.B: Puedo {{plural_you:hablarles|hablaros}} con toda franqueza, y tengo todos los motivos para estar orgulloso de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. El consuelo me llena, y la alegría me desborda a pesar de todas nuestras dificultades.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} hablo con franqueza y sinceridad, y estoy muy orgulloso de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Estoy lleno de consuelo. Aun con todos nuestros problemas, tengo más alegría de la que puedo contener.

sw.L: Ujasiri wangu kwenu [ni] mkubwa; fahari yangu juu yenu [ni] kubwa. Nimejazwa faraja; nimefurika furaha katika dhiki yetu yote.
sw.B: Ninaweza kusema nanyi kwa uwazi mkubwa, na nina kila sababu ya kuona fahari juu yenu. Faraja imenijaa, na furaha inanifurika licha ya dhiki zetu zote.
sw.R: Ninasema nanyi waziwazi na kwa unyofu, nami naona fahari kubwa juu yenu. Nimejaa faraja. Hata katika taabu zetu zote, nina furaha kuliko ninavyoweza kuibeba.

decisions.choice: boldness: open, frank speech
decisions.reason: παρρησία is the freedom to speak openly, as in 3:12. It picks up 6:11, "our mouth has been opened to you". The word can also mean confidence, and Paul is confident about them too (verse 16), but here it pairs with what he says to them.

decisions.choice: boasting: proper pride in the church
decisions.reason: καύχησις here is the good pride of 1:12-14: Paul is proud of the Corinthians and speaks well of them to others, as he did to Titus (verse 14).

decisions.choice: comfort: consolation that also strengthens
decisions.reason: παρακλήσει is the word that runs through 1:3-7 and returns in verses 6-7 and 13: comfort that gives courage to go on. Paul says here what he will explain in verses 5-16.

decisions.choice: in all our affliction: joy in the midst of hardship and in spite of it
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ with the dative marks the circumstances. The affliction is the hardship of verse 5; the joy comes with it, from the news Titus brought.

decisions.choice: overflow beyond measure
decisions.reason: ὑπερπερισσεύομαι is a strengthened form of the verb "to overflow": joy more than full.

decisions.choice: every reason to be proud of you (B); very proud of you (R)
decisions.reason: Following the book-wide choice on boasting, Literal keeps "boasting" and the other levels speak of being proud, since Paul's argument here does not turn on the word itself.

decisions.choice: comfort; affliction (L), hardship (B), troubles (R)
decisions.reason: The same English words as in 1:3-7 keep the link with the opening of the letter.

decisions.choice: more joy than I can hold
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the strengthened verb in plain words (m5).

decisions.choice: se vanter, le sujet de fierté (L); être fier, la fierté (B, R) in chapters 7-9, as in 1:12; se vanter at every level in chapters 10-12
alternatives: se glorifier, le sujet de gloire (L)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the book-wide choice of 1:12, "se vanter" and "sujet de fierté", one word across 1 and 2 Corinthians so that the word can be traced (docs/corinthians-terms.md); Balanced and Readable speak of being proud, as the English does, since this is good pride and the argument does not turn on the word itself. In chapters 10-12 it does, so "se vanter" is kept at every level there.

decisions.choice: le réconfort, réconforter (every level); la détresse (L), les épreuves (B), les difficultés (R) (for chapters 7-11)
decisions.reason: The comfort word includes strengthening as well as consolation (docs/corinthians-terms.md), and "réconforter" says both, where "consoler" speaks only to sorrow. One family is kept at every level, so that the link with 1:3-7 can be followed. French "affliction" means grief rather than hardship, so Literal says "la détresse", as in John 16:33; Balanced and Readable use the everyday words.

source.text: Καὶ γὰρ ἐλθόντων ἡμῶν εἰς Μακεδονίαν οὐδεμίαν ἔσχηκεν ἄνεσιν ἡ σὰρξ ἡμῶν, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι ἔξωθεν μάχαι, ἔσωθεν φόβοι ἀλλ’ ὁ παρακαλῶν τοὺς ταπεινοὺς παρεκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ Τίτου·

records.literal_gloss: For indeed having come of us into Macedonia, no relief has had the flesh of us, but in every [way] being afflicted: outside fights, inside fears; \v 6 but the [one] comforting the lowly comforted us, the God, by the coming of Titus;

en.L: For even when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but [we were] afflicted in every way: fights outside, fears inside. \v 6 But the one who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus.
en.B: Even when we came to Macedonia, there was no relief for us in our human weakness. We met hardship at every turn: strife all around us, fear in our hearts. \v 6 But God, who comforts those who are brought low, comforted us by bringing Titus to us.
en.R: When we came to Macedonia, we still could not rest. We had troubles everywhere. There were fights and quarrels around us, and we were afraid inside. \v 6 But God comforts people who are low and discouraged, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comforted us when Titus came.

fr.L: Car même quand nous sommes arrivés en Macédoine, notre chair n’a eu aucun repos, mais [nous avons été] dans la détresse de toutes les manières : au-dehors des combats, au-dedans des craintes. \v 6 Mais celui qui réconforte les humbles, Dieu, nous a réconfortés par la venue de Tite.
fr.B: Même quand nous sommes arrivés en Macédoine, nous n’avons trouvé aucun répit dans notre faiblesse humaine. Nous rencontrions des épreuves de tous côtés : des conflits autour de nous, de la peur en nous. \v 6 Mais Dieu, qui réconforte ceux qui sont abattus, nous a réconfortés en nous amenant Tite.
fr.R: Quand nous sommes arrivés en Macédoine, nous ne pouvions toujours pas nous reposer. Nous avions des difficultés partout. Il y avait des disputes et des conflits autour de nous, et nous avions peur au fond de nous. \v 6 Mais Dieu réconforte les gens qui sont abattus et découragés, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a réconfortés quand Tite est arrivé.

es.L: Porque, en efecto, cuando llegamos a Macedonia, nuestra carne no tuvo ningún descanso, sino que [fuimos] afligidos en todo: luchas por fuera, temores por dentro. \v 6 Pero el que consuela a los humildes, Dios, nos consoló con la llegada de Tito;
es.B: Aun cuando llegamos a Macedonia, no hubo descanso para nosotros en nuestra debilidad humana. Encontramos dificultades por todas partes: conflictos a nuestro alrededor, temor en nuestro corazón. \v 6 Pero Dios, que consuela a los abatidos, nos consoló trayéndonos a Tito.
es.R: Cuando llegamos a Macedonia, todavía no podíamos descansar. Teníamos problemas por todas partes. Había peleas y discusiones a nuestro alrededor, y por dentro teníamos miedo. \v 6 Pero Dios consuela a los que están tristes y desanimados, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos consoló cuando llegó Tito.

sw.L: Kwa maana hata tulipofika Makedonia, mwili wetu haukupata nafuu, bali [tulikuwa] tukipata dhiki kwa kila namna: nje mapigano, ndani hofu. \v 6 Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayewafariji wanyonge, Mungu, alitufariji kwa kuja kwa Tito.
sw.B: Hata tulipofika Makedonia, hatukupata nafuu katika udhaifu wetu wa kibinadamu. Tulikutana na dhiki kila upande: mapigano kila upande wetu, hofu mioyoni mwetu. \v 6 Lakini Mungu, anayewafariji walioshushwa chini, alitufariji kwa kumleta Tito kwetu.
sw.R: Tulipofika Makedonia, bado hatukuweza kupumzika. Tulikuwa na taabu kila mahali. Kulikuwa na mapigano na magomvi kutuzunguka, na ndani yetu tuliogopa. \v 6 Lakini Mungu huwafariji watu wanyonge na waliokata tamaa, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} alitufariji Tito alipokuja.

decisions.choice: the story of 2:12-13 picks up again
decisions.reason: Καὶ γὰρ ("for indeed") resumes the account Paul broke off at 2:13: he left Troas for Macedonia because he had not found Titus. The long passage 2:14-7:4 comes between.

decisions.choice: our flesh: Paul as a weak human being, the whole self
decisions.reason: σὰρξ here is Paul's frail human existence. It cannot mean the body alone, since the fears in the same verse are inward. In 2:13 he said his spirit had no relief; here he says the same of his whole human self.

decisions.choice: a broken sentence: a participle with no main verb, then two short phrases
alternatives: a smooth sentence with a missing "we were"
decisions.reason: θλιβόμενοι ("being afflicted") does not fit the grammar of the clause before it, and the words that follow are two bare phrases, "outside fights, inside fears". The broken style suits the strain Paul describes.

decisions.choice: conflicts without, fears within
decisions.reason: μάχαι are fights or quarrels: opposition and trouble from outside. φόβοι are Paul's own anxieties, above all about Corinth and about Titus (2:13).

decisions.choice: God who comforts the lowly: an echo of Isaiah 49:13
decisions.reason: In the Greek translation of Isaiah 49:13 God comforts the lowly of his people, with the same words for "comfort" and "lowly". Paul uses it as a title of God (compare 1:3, "the God of all comfort").

decisions.choice: the lowly: those brought low and downcast
decisions.reason: ταπεινοὺς can mean humble in character, but here it means people pressed down by trouble, as Paul was.

decisions.choice: coming: the arrival and presence of Titus
decisions.reason: παρουσίᾳ is used here in its everyday sense, the arrival of a person. Titus came to Paul in Macedonia with news from Corinth.

decisions.choice: afflicted (L), hardship (B), troubles (R); comfort
decisions.reason: The same word families as in 1:3-7 and 7:4.

decisions.choice: in our human weakness
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the book-wide choice of not saying "flesh" and gives the sense of weak human existence (m2).

decisions.choice: But God comforts people who are low and discouraged, and he comforted us
alternatives: the one who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us
decisions.reason: Readable makes the title of God into its own clause.

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level for Paul's account of his arrival in Macedonia (7:5-7), with the imperfect for what went on ("nous rencontrions", "nous avions peur")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, as for Paul's travels in Galatians 1-2
decisions.reason: These verses are not a sustained narrative but Paul telling the church what he felt and how God comforted him, in the middle of speaking to them; the Greek itself uses a perfect ("has had no relief"). French uses the passé composé for that, as for the rest of the letter.

decisions.choice: los abatidos
decisions.reason: Here the word means people brought low by distress, not people who are modest; Literal keeps "humildes", the word's usual sense, and Balanced says "abatidos".

decisions.choice: mwili wetu (L); udhaifu wetu wa kibinadamu (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mwili" (flesh); here it means Paul as a weak human being (meaning decision), so Balanced says "udhaifu wetu wa kibinadamu", as the English Balanced does.

source.text: οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει ᾗ παρεκλήθη ἐφ’ ὑμῖν, ἀναγγέλλων ἡμῖν τὴν ὑμῶν ἐπιπόθησιν, τὸν ὑμῶν ὀδυρμόν, τὸν ὑμῶν ζῆλον ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ, ὥστε με μᾶλλον χαρῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: not only and by the coming of him, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted over you, reporting to us the your longing, the your lament, the your zeal for me, so that me the more to rejoice.

en.L: And not only by his coming, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted over you, as he reported to us your longing, your lament, your zeal on my behalf, so that I rejoiced all the more.
en.B: And it was not only his arrival that comforted us, but also the comfort he himself had found among you. He told us how you long for me, how you mourn over what happened, how eager you are to stand up for me. So my joy was greater still.
en.R: It was not only that Titus came. He told us how much you had comforted him. He said that you want very much to see me, that you are very sorry about what happened, and that you care deeply about me. That made me even more glad.

fr.L: Et non seulement par sa venue, mais aussi par le réconfort dont il a été réconforté à votre sujet, quand il nous a rapporté votre vif désir, votre lamentation, votre zèle pour moi, de sorte que je me suis réjoui davantage.
fr.B: Et ce n’est pas seulement son arrivée qui nous a réconfortés, mais aussi le réconfort qu’il avait lui-même trouvé auprès de vous. Il nous a dit combien vous désirez me revoir, combien vous pleurez sur ce qui s’est passé, avec quelle ardeur vous prenez mon parti. Ma joie en a été plus grande encore.
fr.R: Il n’y a pas seulement eu l’arrivée de Tite. Il nous a raconté combien vous l’aviez réconforté. Il nous a dit que vous désirez beaucoup me voir, que vous êtes désolés de ce qui s’est passé, et que vous tenez beaucoup à moi. Cela m’a rendu encore plus heureux.

es.L: y no solo con su llegada, sino también con el consuelo con que él fue consolado en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, al contarnos {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} anhelo, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} llanto, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} celo por mí, de modo que me alegré aún más.
es.B: Y no fue solo su llegada lo que nos consoló, sino también el consuelo que él mismo había encontrado entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Nos contó cuánto {{plural_you:me añoran|me añoráis}}, cómo {{plural_you:lloran|lloráis}} por lo sucedido y con qué celo {{plural_you:están|estáis}} dispuestos a defenderme. Así que mi alegría fue todavía mayor.
es.R: No fue solo que llegó Tito. Él nos contó cuánto lo {{plural_you:habían|habíais}} consolado {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Nos dijo que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} muchas ganas de verme, que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} muy dolidos por lo que pasó y que {{plural_you:se preocupan|os preocupáis}} mucho por mí. Eso me alegró todavía más.

sw.L: na si kwa kuja kwake tu, bali pia kwa faraja aliyofarijiwa nayo kwenu, alipotueleza shauku yenu, maombolezo yenu, bidii yenu kwa ajili yangu, hata nikazidi kufurahi.
sw.B: Wala si kuja kwake tu kulikotufariji, bali pia faraja aliyokuwa ameipata kwenu. Alitueleza jinsi mnavyonitamani, jinsi mnavyoomboleza kwa yaliyotokea, jinsi mlivyo na bidii ya kunitetea. Kwa hiyo furaha yangu ikazidi zaidi.
sw.R: Haikuwa tu kwamba Tito alikuja. Alitueleza jinsi mlivyomfariji sana. Alisema kwamba mnatamani sana kuniona, kwamba mnasikitika sana kwa yaliyotokea, na kwamba mnanijali sana. Hilo lilinifurahisha zaidi.

decisions.choice: Titus had been comforted by the Corinthians' response
alternatives: Titus was comforted about them by God
decisions.reason: ἐφ ὑμῖν ("over you") names what comforted Titus: the way the church received him and the letter. His comfort became Paul's.

decisions.choice: longing: a longing to see Paul and be reconciled with him
alternatives: a longing for the offender to be punished
decisions.reason: ἐπιπόθησιν is an eager desire. After the painful visit and the letter, the church longed to see Paul again (compare verse 11).

decisions.choice: lament: sorrow over what had happened
decisions.reason: ὀδυρμόν is loud grief or lament. Here it is the church's sorrow over the wrong done and the break with Paul.

decisions.choice: "for me" goes most clearly with zeal, and colors all three
decisions.reason: ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ("for me") stands after the third noun. The zeal was on Paul's side, eagerness to take his part; the longing and the lament also concern him.

decisions.choice: over what happened (B); about what happened (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the church was mourning (m3).

decisions.choice: comfort; lament (L), mourn (B), sorry (R)
decisions.reason: The word for lament is not the word for grief in verses 8-11, so it is kept apart from grief and sadness.

decisions.choice: votre lamentation (L); vous pleurez (B); vous êtes désolés (R)
decisions.reason: The word for lament is not the grief word of verses 8-11, so it is kept apart from "tristesse" and "triste" at every level, and from "regretter", which renders the verb for regret in verse 8.

decisions.choice: lloran por lo sucedido (B); están muy dolidos por lo que pasó (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "sorry"; Spanish "arrepentidos" would bring in the repentance word of verses 9-10, so Readable says "dolidos" for their sorrow.

decisions.choice: shauku; maombolezo; bidii
decisions.reason: "Shauku" is longing, "maombolezo" mourning, and "bidii" eager devotion, as Romans 10:2 renders the same zeal word; "wivu" now means jealousy. The same three words return in 7:11.

source.text: ὅτι εἰ καὶ ἐλύπησα ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ, οὐ μεταμέλομαι· εἰ καὶ μετεμελόμην βλέπω ὅτι ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἐκείνη εἰ καὶ πρὸς ὥραν ἐλύπησεν ὑμᾶς, νῦν χαίρω, οὐχ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε, ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε εἰς μετάνοιαν, ἐλυπήθητε γὰρ κατὰ θεόν, ἵνα ἐν μηδενὶ ζημιωθῆτε ἐξ ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Because if even I grieved you by the letter, not I regret [it]; if even I was regretting [it] - I see that the letter that, if even for an hour, grieved you - \v 9 now I rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved unto repentance; for you were grieved according to God, so that in nothing you might suffer loss from us.

en.L: For even if I grieved you by the letter, I do not regret [it]. Though I did regret [it] (I see that that letter grieved you, if only for an hour), \v 9 now I rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved to repentance; for you were grieved according to God, so that you would suffer loss from us in nothing.
en.B: So even if my letter grieved you, I do not regret it. I did regret it for a while, for I see that the letter grieved you, if only for a short time. \v 9 Now, though, I rejoice. It is not your grief that makes me glad, but the fact that it brought you to repentance. You grieved in God's way, and so you have lost nothing because of us.
en.R: Even if my letter made you sad, I am not sorry I sent it. For a while I was sorry, because I knew the letter made you sad, even if only for a short time. \v 9 But now I am glad. I am not glad that you were sad. I am glad because your sadness made you turn away from what was wrong. You were sad in the way God wants, so we did not harm you at all.

fr.L: Car même si je vous ai attristés par la lettre, je ne [le] regrette pas. Même si je [le] regrettais (je vois que cette lettre vous a attristés, ne serait-ce que pour une heure), \v 9 maintenant je me réjouis, non de ce que vous avez été attristés, mais de ce que vous avez été attristés jusqu’à la repentance ; car vous avez été attristés selon Dieu, afin de ne subir de notre part aucun dommage.
fr.B: Ainsi, même si ma lettre vous a attristés, je ne le regrette pas. Je l’ai regretté un moment, car je vois que cette lettre vous a attristés, même si ce n’a été que pour peu de temps. \v 9 Maintenant pourtant, je me réjouis. Ce n’est pas votre tristesse qui me rend heureux, mais le fait qu’elle vous a conduits à la repentance. Votre tristesse était selon la volonté de Dieu, et ainsi vous n’avez rien perdu à cause de nous.
fr.R: Même si ma lettre vous a rendus tristes, je ne regrette pas de l’avoir envoyée. Pendant un moment, je l’ai regretté, parce que je savais que la lettre vous avait rendus tristes, même si ce n’était que pour peu de temps. \v 9 Mais maintenant, je suis heureux. Je ne suis pas heureux que vous ayez été tristes. Je suis heureux parce que votre tristesse vous a poussés à vous détourner de ce qui était mal. Vous avez été tristes comme Dieu le veut, et ainsi nous ne vous avons fait aucun tort.

es.L: Porque, aunque {{plural_you:los|os}} entristecí con la carta, no lo lamento. Aunque sí lo lamentaba (veo que aquella carta {{plural_you:los|os}} entristeció, aunque solo por un tiempo), \v 9 ahora me alegro, no porque {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} entristecidos, sino porque {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} entristecidos para arrepentimiento; porque {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} entristecidos según Dios, para que en nada {{plural_you:sufrieran|sufrierais}} pérdida por nuestra parte.
es.B: Así que, aunque mi carta {{plural_you:los|os}} entristeció, no lo lamento. Sí lo lamenté por un tiempo, porque veo que la carta {{plural_you:los|os}} entristeció, aunque fuera por poco tiempo. \v 9 Pero ahora me alegro. No me alegra que {{plural_you:estuvieran|estuvierais}} tristes, sino que esa tristeza {{plural_you:los|os}} llevó al arrepentimiento. {{plural_you:Se entristecieron|Os entristecisteis}} como Dios quiere, y así no {{plural_you:han perdido|habéis perdido}} nada por causa nuestra.
es.R: Aunque mi carta {{plural_you:los|os}} puso tristes, no siento haberla enviado. Por un tiempo sí lo sentí, porque sabía que la carta {{plural_you:los|os}} había puesto tristes, aunque fuera por poco tiempo. \v 9 Pero ahora estoy contento. No estoy contento porque {{plural_you:estuvieron|estuvisteis}} tristes. Estoy contento porque {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tristeza {{plural_you:los hizo apartarse|os hizo apartaros}} de lo que estaba mal. {{plural_you:Estuvieron|Estuvisteis}} tristes de la manera que Dios quiere, así que no {{plural_you:les|os}} hicimos ningún daño.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hata ikiwa niliwahuzunisha kwa ile barua, sijutii; hata kama nilijutia (naona kwamba barua ile iliwahuzunisha, ingawa kwa saa moja tu), \v 9 sasa nafurahi, si kwa sababu mlihuzunishwa, bali kwa sababu mlihuzunishwa hata mkafikia toba; kwa maana mlihuzunishwa kwa jinsi ya Mungu, ili msipate hasara kwetu katika jambo lolote.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hata ikiwa barua yangu iliwahuzunisha, sijutii. Nilijutia kwa muda, kwa sababu naona kwamba barua ile iliwahuzunisha, ingawa kwa muda mfupi tu. \v 9 Lakini sasa nafurahi. Si huzuni yenu inayonifurahisha, bali ukweli kwamba iliwaleta kwenye toba. Mlihuzunika kwa jinsi ya Mungu, na kwa hiyo hamkupata hasara yoyote kwa sababu yetu.
sw.R: Hata ikiwa barua yangu iliwahuzunisha, sijutii kuituma. Kwa muda nilijuta, kwa sababu nilijua barua ile iliwahuzunisha, ingawa kwa muda mfupi tu. \v 9 Lakini sasa nafurahi. Sifurahi kwa sababu mlihuzunika. Nafurahi kwa sababu huzuni yenu iliwafanya mgeuke na kuacha yale yaliyokuwa mabaya. Mlihuzunika kwa jinsi Mungu anavyotaka, kwa hiyo hatukuwadhuru hata kidogo.

decisions.choice: the letter: the earlier, tearful letter of 2:3-4, not this letter
decisions.reason: This is the letter of 2:3-4 and 2:9, written "with many tears" in place of a visit; "that letter" sets it apart from the one Paul is writing now. Whether it is 1 Corinthians or a letter that has not survived cannot be settled from the text. 1 Corinthians does not read like a letter written in tears, so many readers think of a lost letter.

decisions.choice: "though I did regret it" goes with "now I rejoice"; "I see that ..." is an aside
alternatives: "I do not regret it, though I did regret it." as one sentence, with a new sentence beginning "I see"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuation ties the second "if" clause to νῦν χαίρω ("now I rejoice"): though Paul once regretted sending the letter, he is glad now. The words about seeing that the letter grieved them break in to explain why he had regretted it. Other editions end a sentence after the second regret.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "I see" without "for"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "for I see", which makes the aside a reason for the regret; others lack "for". The SBLGNT prints the shorter text. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: regret: to be sorry about something one has done
decisions.reason: μεταμέλομαι is to feel regret about a past action, here about sending a severe letter. It is a different word from the repentance of verse 9, though verse 10 plays on the two.

decisions.choice: repentance: a change of heart and mind that turns from wrong and acts on it
decisions.reason: μετάνοιαν is more than feeling sorry: it is a turning that changes what one does. Here it is the church's change of mind about the wrong done and about Paul, shown in the actions of verse 11. They were already believers, so this is not their first turning to God.

decisions.choice: grieved according to God: grief that follows God's will and turns toward him
decisions.reason: κατὰ θεόν ("according to God") describes the kind of grief: the grief God desires, felt before him. Verse 10 sets it against "the world's grief".

decisions.choice: result: the letter did the church no harm
alternatives: purpose: so that Paul would not have to punish them in person
decisions.reason: ἵνα with the subjunctive here states what followed from God's purpose: the painful letter did them no damage but good. Some take it as Paul's aim of sparing them a harsher visit (compare 1:23), which comes to the same thing.

decisions.choice: grieve (L, B); sad (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:1-7, Literal and Balanced keep the grief family and Readable the sad family, so that the reader can follow the word through verses 8-11.

decisions.choice: repentance (L, B); turn away from what was wrong (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the familiar word. Readable says what it means in this setting, since "repent" may be church language to a young reader (m5).

decisions.choice: in God's way (B); in the way God wants (R)
decisions.reason: The same English phrase is used in verses 9, 10 and 11 so that the contrast with the world's grief stays visible.

decisions.choice: sorry
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for regret.

decisions.choice: attrister, la tristesse (L, B); rendre triste, triste (R); la repentance (L, B), vous détourner de ce qui était mal (R)
decisions.reason: One family for the grief word at each level, so that the reader can follow it through verses 8-11, as the English does. "La repentance" is the term the style guide sets; Readable says what it means here, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: selon Dieu (L); selon la volonté de Dieu (B); comme Dieu le veut (R), the same in verses 9, 10 and 11
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly that this grief follows God's will (m6), since "selon Dieu" alone is church language; each level repeats its phrase in verses 9-11 so that the contrast with the world's grief stays visible.

decisions.choice: lamentar (L, B); sentir (R)
decisions.reason: This verb is regret, not the repentance of verses 9-10, and the Spanish word list keeps "arrepentirse" away from it; "lamentar" and the everyday "sentir" say regret without that confusion.

decisions.choice: arrepentimiento (L, B); apartarse de lo que estaba mal (R)
decisions.reason: "Arrepentimiento" is the word used for repentance in the Spanish already drafted; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: toba (L, B); mgeuke na kuacha yale yaliyokuwa mabaya (R)
decisions.reason: "Toba" is the Swahili word for repentance, turning from wrong; "majuto" (regret) is kept for the different verb "kujuta" in verses 8 and 10, so the two are not confused. Readable explains, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: kujuta / kujutia
decisions.reason: "Kujuta" is to be sorry for something one has done, the sense of the meaning decision; Readable keeps it, since it is everyday Swahili.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ κατὰ θεὸν λύπη μετάνοιαν εἰς σωτηρίαν ἀμεταμέλητον ἐργάζεται· ἡ δὲ τοῦ κόσμου λύπη θάνατον κατεργάζεται.

records.literal_gloss: The for according to God grief repentance unto salvation not to be regretted works; the but of the world grief death works out.

en.L: For the grief according to God works repentance unto salvation, not to be regretted; but the grief of the world works out death.
en.B: Grief that follows God's way produces repentance that leads to salvation, a repentance no one will ever regret. But grief that follows the world's way produces death.
en.R: When people are sad in the way God wants, it makes them turn away from what is wrong. That leads to salvation, and no one is ever sorry about that. But the kind of sadness the world has leads to death.

fr.L: Car la tristesse selon Dieu produit une repentance en vue du salut, qu’on ne regrette pas ; mais la tristesse du monde produit la mort.
fr.B: La tristesse selon la volonté de Dieu produit une repentance qui mène au salut, une repentance que personne ne regrettera jamais. Mais la tristesse selon le monde produit la mort.
fr.R: Quand les gens sont tristes comme Dieu le veut, cela les pousse à se détourner de ce qui est mal. Cela conduit au salut, et personne ne le regrette jamais. Mais la tristesse que connaît le monde conduit à la mort.

es.L: Porque la tristeza según Dios produce arrepentimiento para salvación, del que no hay que lamentarse; pero la tristeza del mundo produce muerte.
es.B: La tristeza que es como Dios quiere produce un arrepentimiento que lleva a la salvación, un arrepentimiento que nadie lamentará jamás. Pero la tristeza que es como la del mundo produce muerte.
es.R: Cuando las personas están tristes de la manera que Dios quiere, eso las hace apartarse de lo malo. Eso lleva a la salvación, y nadie lo lamenta nunca. Pero la clase de tristeza que tiene el mundo lleva a la muerte.

sw.L: Kwa maana huzuni iliyo kwa jinsi ya Mungu huleta toba iletayo wokovu, isiyojutiwa; lakini huzuni ya ulimwengu huleta kifo.
sw.B: Huzuni inayofuata njia ya Mungu huleta toba iongozayo kwenye wokovu, toba ambayo hakuna mtu atakayeijutia kamwe. Lakini huzuni inayofuata njia ya ulimwengu huleta kifo.
sw.R: Watu wanapohuzunika kwa jinsi Mungu anavyotaka, huzuni hiyo huwafanya waache yale yaliyo mabaya. Hilo huleta wokovu, na hakuna mtu anayejuta kamwe kwa ajili ya hilo. Lakini huzuni ya namna ya ulimwengu huleta kifo.

decisions.choice: two kinds of grief: grief before God and grief as the world knows it
alternatives: grief sent by God and grief sent by the world
decisions.reason: κατὰ θεὸν ("according to God") and τοῦ κόσμου ("of the world") describe the character of the grief, not who sends it. One looks to God and leads to change; the other stays shut up in itself.

decisions.choice: "not to be regretted" describes the repentance, and with it the salvation it leads to
decisions.reason: ἀμεταμέλητον follows "salvation" but most likely goes with repentance, playing on the regret of verse 8: Paul once regretted the letter, but no one regrets this kind of repentance. Either way the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the world: human life lived apart from God
decisions.reason: κόσμου here is the world in its turning away from God. Its grief is sorrow that has no turning to God in it: remorse, self-pity or bitterness.

decisions.choice: salvation and death: the two ends to which the two kinds of grief lead
decisions.reason: σωτηρίαν is God's full rescue; θάνατον is its opposite, ruin and separation from God. Grief without repentance does not merely fail to help; it harms.

decisions.choice: works, works out: brings about, produces
decisions.reason: ἐργάζεται and the stronger κατεργάζεται both mean to bring something about. The second is used again in verse 11 for what grief worked in the church.

decisions.choice: grief that follows God's way ... the world's way (B); sad in the way God wants ... the kind of sadness the world has (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of grief is meant (m1) and keep the same phrase as in verses 9 and 11. Readable uses the sad family, as in verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: turn away from what is wrong
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, Readable says what repentance means here.

source.text: ἰδοὺ γὰρ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ κατὰ θεὸν λυπηθῆναι πόσην κατειργάσατο ὑμῖν σπουδήν, ἀλλὰ ἀπολογίαν, ἀλλὰ ἀγανάκτησιν, ἀλλὰ φόβον, ἀλλὰ ἐπιπόθησιν, ἀλλὰ ζῆλον, ἀλλὰ ἐκδίκησιν· ἐν παντὶ συνεστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς ἁγνοὺς εἶναι τῷ πράγματι.

records.literal_gloss: For look, this very thing, the according to God to be grieved, how much it worked in you earnestness, but defense, but indignation, but fear, but longing, but zeal, but punishment; in everything you showed yourselves innocent to be in the matter.

en.L: For look at this very thing, being grieved according to God: how much earnestness it worked in you; yes, defense; yes, indignation; yes, fear; yes, longing; yes, zeal; yes, punishment! In everything you have shown yourselves to be innocent in the matter.
en.B: Think what this grieving in God's way has done for you! How earnest it has made you, how eager to clear yourselves, how indignant, how alarmed, how full of longing, how zealous, how ready to see the wrong punished! In everything you have shown that you are clear of blame in this affair.
en.R: Look at what this sadness, the kind God wants, has done in you! Now you are serious about doing what is right. You want to show that you were not to blame. You are angry about what happened, and you are afraid of what might happen. You long to see me, and you care deeply. You are ready to make sure the wrong is punished. In every way you have shown that you have done nothing wrong in this matter.

fr.L: Car voici, cela même, être attristés selon Dieu, quel empressement cela a produit en vous ; oui, quelle défense ; oui, quelle indignation ; oui, quelle crainte ; oui, quel désir ; oui, quel zèle ; oui, quelle punition ! En tout, vous vous êtes montrés innocents dans cette affaire.
fr.B: Voyez ce que cette tristesse selon la volonté de Dieu a fait pour vous ! Quel sérieux elle a fait naître en vous, quel empressement à vous justifier, quelle indignation, quelle inquiétude, quel désir ardent, quel zèle, quelle volonté de voir le mal puni ! En tout, vous avez montré que vous n’avez rien à vous reprocher dans cette affaire.
fr.R: Regardez ce que cette tristesse, celle que Dieu veut, a fait en vous ! Maintenant, vous voulez sérieusement faire ce qui est juste. Vous voulez montrer que vous n’étiez pas coupables. Vous êtes en colère à cause de ce qui s’est passé, et vous avez peur de ce qui pourrait arriver. Vous désirez me voir, et vous tenez beaucoup à moi. Vous êtes prêts à faire en sorte que le mal soit puni. De toutes les manières, vous avez montré que vous n’avez rien fait de mal dans cette affaire.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} esto mismo, el ser entristecidos según Dios: ¡cuánta diligencia produjo en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; sí, defensa; sí, indignación; sí, temor; sí, anhelo; sí, celo; sí, castigo! En todo {{plural_you:se han mostrado|os habéis mostrado}} inocentes en el asunto.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} lo que ha hecho en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} esta tristeza según Dios! ¡Qué empeño ha producido en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, qué deseo de {{plural_you:justificarse|justificaros}}, qué indignación, qué temor, qué anhelo, qué celo, qué disposición a castigar el mal! En todo {{plural_you:han demostrado|habéis demostrado}} que no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} culpa en este asunto.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} lo que esta tristeza, la que Dios quiere, ha hecho en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! Ahora {{plural_you:toman|tomáis}} en serio hacer lo correcto. {{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} mostrar que no {{plural_you:tenían|teníais}} la culpa. {{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} enojados por lo que pasó, y {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} miedo de lo que podría pasar. {{plural_you:Desean|Deseáis}} verme, y {{plural_you:se preocupan|os preocupáis}} de verdad. {{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} dispuestos a asegurar que el mal sea castigado. En todo {{plural_you:han mostrado|habéis mostrado}} que no {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} nada malo en este asunto.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama jambo hili hili, kuhuzunishwa kwa jinsi ya Mungu: jinsi lilivyotenda ndani yenu juhudi kubwa; naam, kujitetea; naam, hasira; naam, hofu; naam, shauku; naam, bidii; naam, adhabu! Katika kila jambo mmejionyesha kuwa safi katika jambo hilo.
sw.B: Fikirini jambo hili la kuhuzunika kwa jinsi ya Mungu limewafanyia nini! Limewafanya kuwa na juhudi kiasi gani, hamu kiasi gani ya kujisafisha, hasira kiasi gani, hofu kiasi gani, shauku kiasi gani, bidii kiasi gani, utayari kiasi gani wa kuona kosa likiadhibiwa! Katika kila jambo mmeonyesha kwamba hamna lawama katika suala hili.
sw.R: Tazameni huzuni hii, ya aina anayoitaka Mungu, imefanya nini ndani yenu! Sasa mko makini kufanya yaliyo sawa. Mnataka kuonyesha kwamba hamkuwa na hatia. Mmekasirika kwa yaliyotokea, na mnaogopa yanayoweza kutokea. Mnatamani kuniona, na mnajali sana. Mko tayari kuhakikisha kwamba kosa linaadhibiwa. Kwa kila namna mmeonyesha kwamba hamkufanya kosa lolote katika jambo hili.

decisions.choice: "but" repeated: "yes, and more"
decisions.reason: ἀλλὰ usually means "but". Repeated before each noun, it adds and heightens: "and not only that, but also". The list piles up what grief in God's way produced.

decisions.choice: earnestness: eager seriousness to put things right
decisions.reason: σπουδήν is zeal and earnest effort. It heads the list, and verse 12 says the letter's aim was to bring it into the open.

decisions.choice: defense: eagerness to clear themselves
decisions.reason: ἀπολογίαν is a speech of defense. The church was eager to show that it did not side with the wrong.

decisions.choice: indignation at the wrong; fear of the consequences
decisions.reason: ἀγανάκτησιν is anger at something shameful, here at the wrong done, and perhaps at themselves for allowing it. φόβον is most likely alarm at Paul's coming and reverent fear before God, who judges.

decisions.choice: longing for Paul; zeal for him
decisions.reason: The same two words appear in verse 7, where they are "for me". So the longing is to see Paul, and the zeal is eagerness to take his part.

decisions.choice: punishment: seeing that the wrong is dealt with
decisions.reason: ἐκδίκησιν means doing justice or punishing a wrong. It is the church's discipline of the offender (2:6), not personal revenge.

decisions.choice: innocent in the matter: the church as a whole had no part in the wrong
alternatives: the church had been guilty but is now forgiven
decisions.reason: ἁγνοὺς means pure or innocent. By how they acted the Corinthians showed that they did not share in the wrong done; πράγματι is the affair Paul does not name.

decisions.choice: a string of exclamations: how earnest ... how ready
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the nouns into adjectives and phrases so that the list reads naturally while keeping its building force (m1).

decisions.choice: Now you are serious about doing what is right ... You are ready to make sure the wrong is punished
decisions.reason: Readable turns each noun into a short sentence and says what it refers to (m2-m6). "Afraid of what might happen" and "long to see me" fill in objects the Greek leaves unstated.

decisions.choice: naam
decisions.reason: The repeated Greek word means "yes, and more" here (meaning decision); "naam" (yes indeed) says that, where "lakini" (but) would set the items against each other.

decisions.choice: hasira
decisions.reason: "Ghadhabu" is kept for God's wrath (Romans 1:18), so the church's indignation at the wrong is "hasira".

source.text: ἄρα εἰ καὶ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, οὐχ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικήσαντος, οὐδὲ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικηθέντος, ἀλλ’ ἕνεκεν τοῦ φανερωθῆναι τὴν σπουδὴν ὑμῶν τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So if even I wrote to you, not for the sake of the [one] having done wrong, nor for the sake of the [one] having been wronged, but for the sake of the to be made manifest the earnestness of you, the [one] on behalf of us, to you before the God.

en.L: So even though I wrote to you, [it was] not for the sake of the one who did wrong, nor for the sake of the one who was wronged, but for the sake of your earnestness on our behalf being made manifest to you before God.
en.B: So although I wrote to you, my aim was not the man who did the wrong, nor the one who was wronged. I wrote so that your earnest care for us would become plain to you yourselves, there in the sight of God.
en.R: So yes, I did write that letter to you. But I did not write it mainly because of the man who did wrong, or because of the one he hurt. I wrote it so that you would see for yourselves, with God watching, how much you really care about us.

fr.L: Ainsi, même si je vous ai écrit, [ce n’était] pas à cause de celui qui a commis le tort, ni à cause de celui qui l’a subi, mais pour que votre empressement pour nous soit rendu manifeste auprès de vous devant Dieu.
fr.B: Ainsi, quand je vous ai écrit, je ne visais ni l’homme qui a commis le tort, ni celui qui l’a subi. J’ai écrit pour que votre zèle pour nous devienne évident à vos propres yeux, sous le regard de Dieu.
fr.R: Alors oui, je vous ai bien écrit cette lettre. Mais je ne l’ai pas écrite surtout à cause de l’homme qui a mal agi, ou à cause de celui à qui il a fait du tort. Je l’ai écrite pour que vous voyiez vous-mêmes, sous le regard de Dieu, combien vous tenez vraiment à nous.

es.L: Así que, aunque {{plural_you:les|os}} escribí, [no fue] por causa del que cometió el agravio, ni por causa del que fue agraviado, sino para que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} diligencia por nosotros se manifestara ante {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} delante de Dios.
es.B: Así que, aunque {{plural_you:les|os}} escribí, mi propósito no era el hombre que cometió el agravio, ni el que lo sufrió. Escribí para que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} solicitud por nosotros quedara clara ante {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos, allí en la presencia de Dios.
es.R: Así que, sí, {{plural_you:les|os}} escribí aquella carta. Pero no la escribí sobre todo por el hombre que hizo el mal, ni por aquel a quien hizo daño. La escribí para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:vieran|vierais}}, con Dios como testigo, cuánto {{plural_you:se preocupan|os preocupáis}} de verdad por nosotros.

sw.L: Basi hata kama niliwaandikia, [haikuwa] kwa ajili ya yule aliyetenda kosa, wala kwa ajili ya yule aliyetendewa kosa, bali ili juhudi yenu kwa ajili yetu idhihirishwe kwenu mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, ingawa niliwaandikia, kusudi langu halikuwa yule mtu aliyetenda kosa, wala yule aliyetendewa kosa. Niliandika ili juhudi yenu ya kutujali iwe wazi kwenu ninyi wenyewe, mbele za Mungu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo ndiyo, niliwaandikia ile barua. Lakini sikuiandika hasa kwa sababu ya mtu aliyetenda kosa, au kwa sababu ya yule aliyekosewa. Niliiandika ili mjionee wenyewe, Mungu akiwa anaona, jinsi mnavyotujali kweli.

decisions.choice: "I wrote": the same earlier letter as in verse 8 and 2:3-4
decisions.reason: The letter is the one that grieved them (verse 8) and the tearful letter of 2:3-4 and 2:9. Whether it is 1 Corinthians or a lost letter cannot be settled from the text.

decisions.choice: the wrongdoer is the offender of 2:5-11; the one wronged is probably Paul himself
alternatives: a church member wronged by him
decisions.reason: Both are masculine singulars and point to particular people Paul does not name. ἀδικήσαντος is the man of 2:5-11, whom the church disciplined. ἀδικηθέντος may be Paul, insulted or opposed on his painful visit (2:1), which would explain his grief and his careful "not me" in 2:5. Some think of another member of the church; those who link the case with 1 Corinthians 5:1 think of the man's father.

decisions.choice: "not ... but": not chiefly for them, but above all for this
alternatives: Paul did not care about either man
decisions.reason: A Hebrew and Greek way of stressing one thing is to deny the other. Paul did care about both (2:7-10), but the letter's main aim was to bring the church's loyalty into the open.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "your earnestness for us"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts swap the pronouns and read "our earnestness for you", which would make the letter show Paul's care for them. The SBLGNT reads "your earnestness for us", which fits verses 7 and 11. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: made known to you yourselves, under the eyes of God
alternatives: made known to others about you
decisions.reason: πρὸς ὑμᾶς ("to you") means that the church itself would see how loyal it was. ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ("before God") adds that God sees it too, as in 2:17 and 4:2.

decisions.choice: the man (no gender setting)
decisions.reason: The Greek is masculine and means one particular man, as in 2:5-11, so no gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: my aim was not
alternatives: it was not for the sake of
decisions.reason: Balanced says plainly that Paul is speaking of the letter's purpose (m3).

decisions.choice: mainly
decisions.reason: Readable says "mainly" so that Paul does not seem to care nothing for either man (m3).

records.literal_gloss: Because of this we have been comforted.

en.L: For this reason we have been comforted.
en.B: That is why we have been comforted.
en.R: That is why we feel so comforted.

fr.L: À cause de cela, nous avons été réconfortés.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi nous avons été réconfortés.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que nous nous sentons si réconfortés.

es.R: Por eso nos sentimos tan consolados.

decisions.choice: "because of this": the church's response described in verses 11-12
decisions.reason: διὰ τοῦτο looks back: the church's earnest loyalty, now made plain, is what comforted Paul.

decisions.choice: the perfect tense: comfort received and still felt
decisions.reason: παρακεκλήμεθα is perfect: Paul was comforted when Titus came, and the comfort lasts.

decisions.choice: comforted
decisions.reason: The comfort word family stays "comfort" at every level, as in 1:3-7 and verses 4-7.

source.text: Ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ παρακλήσει ἡμῶν περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον ἐχάρημεν ἐπὶ τῇ χαρᾷ Τίτου, ὅτι ἀναπέπαυται τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ πάντων ὑμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: And besides the comfort of us, more abundantly rather we rejoiced at the joy of Titus, because has been refreshed the spirit of him by all of you;

en.L: And besides our comfort, we rejoiced still more abundantly at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
en.B: And on top of our own comfort, we rejoiced even more over the joy Titus had, because all of you had put his spirit at ease.
en.R: We were comforted, and on top of that, we were even more glad because Titus was so full of joy. All of you had cheered him up and put his mind at rest.

fr.L: Et en plus de notre réconfort, nous nous sommes réjouis bien plus encore de la joie de Tite, parce que son esprit a été soulagé par vous tous.
fr.B: Et en plus de notre propre réconfort, nous nous sommes réjouis davantage encore de la joie de Tite, parce que vous tous avez apaisé son esprit.
fr.R: Nous avons été réconfortés, et en plus, nous avons été encore plus heureux parce que Tite était plein de joie. Vous tous lui aviez redonné courage et l’aviez rassuré.

es.L: Y además de nuestro consuelo, nos alegramos aún mucho más por el gozo de Tito, porque su espíritu ha sido confortado por todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Y además de nuestro propio consuelo, nos alegramos todavía más por la alegría que tenía Tito, porque todos {{plural_you:ustedes habían|vosotros habíais}} tranquilizado su espíritu.
es.R: Nos sentimos consolados, y además nos alegramos todavía más porque Tito estaba muy contento. Todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo {{plural_you:habían animado|habíais animado}} y le {{plural_you:habían dado|habíais dado}} tranquilidad.

sw.L: Na zaidi ya faraja yetu, tulifurahi zaidi sana kwa furaha ya Tito, kwa sababu roho yake imeburudishwa na ninyi nyote;
sw.B: Na juu ya faraja yetu wenyewe, tulifurahi hata zaidi kwa furaha aliyokuwa nayo Tito, kwa sababu ninyi nyote mliituliza roho yake.
sw.R: Tulifarijiwa, na zaidi ya hayo, tulifurahi hata zaidi kwa sababu Tito alikuwa amejaa furaha. Ninyi nyote mlikuwa mmemtia moyo na kumpa amani moyoni.

decisions.choice: a doubled comparative: far more still
decisions.reason: περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον are two words for "more" set side by side for emphasis: Titus's joy added a still greater joy to Paul's comfort.

decisions.choice: refreshed: given rest and relief
decisions.reason: ἀναπέπαυται means to give rest. Titus too had gone to Corinth anxious, and the church set him at rest. The perfect tense means the effect lasts.

decisions.choice: spirit: Titus's inner self
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα here is the human spirit, as in 2:13, where Paul's own spirit had no relief.

decisions.choice: by all of you: the whole church shared in it
decisions.reason: πάντων ("all") recurs in verse 15; in 2:6 only the majority had acted, but here the whole church is in view.

decisions.choice: put his spirit at ease
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an active clause and an everyday phrase for being given rest.

decisions.choice: cheered him up and put his mind at rest
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the Greek in plain words.

decisions.choice: soulagé (L); apaisé (B); redonné courage, rassuré (R)
decisions.reason: "Réconforter" is kept for the comfort word of the same verse, so the verb for being given rest takes other words; Literal follows the French of Philemon 7 and 20 for this verb.

source.text: ὅτι εἴ τι αὐτῷ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κεκαύχημαι, οὐ κατῃσχύνθην, ἀλλ’ ὡς πάντα ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ἐλαλήσαμεν ὑμῖν, οὕτως καὶ ἡ καύχησις ἡμῶν ἡ ἐπὶ Τίτου ἀλήθεια ἐγενήθη.

records.literal_gloss: Because if anything to him about you I have boasted, not I was put to shame, but as all things in truth we spoke to you, so also the boasting of us, the [one] before Titus, truth became.

en.L: For if I have boasted anything to him about you, I was not put to shame; but as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting before Titus has proved [to be] truth.
en.B: I had spoken proudly of you to him, and you did not let me down. We have always spoken the truth to you, and in the same way the proud things we said about you to Titus have turned out to be the truth.
en.R: I had told Titus how proud I was of you, and you did not make me look foolish. We have always told you the truth. And when we told Titus how proud we were of you, that turned out to be the truth too.

fr.L: Car si je me suis vanté de quelque chose à votre sujet auprès de lui, je n’ai pas été couvert de honte ; mais comme nous vous avons dit toutes choses en vérité, ainsi notre sujet de fierté devant Tite s’est aussi révélé vérité.
fr.B: J’avais parlé de vous à Tite avec fierté, et vous ne m’avez pas fait honte. Nous vous avons toujours dit la vérité ; de la même façon, ce que nous avons dit de vous à Tite avec fierté s’est révélé vrai.
fr.R: J’avais dit à Tite combien j’étais fier de vous, et grâce à vous, je n’ai pas eu l’air ridicule. Nous vous avons toujours dit la vérité. Et quand nous avons dit à Tite combien nous étions fiers de vous, cela aussi s’est révélé vrai.

es.L: Porque si en algo me he gloriado ante él respecto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no fui avergonzado; sino que, así como {{plural_you:les|os}} hemos dicho todo con verdad, así también nuestro gloriarnos ante Tito resultó [ser] verdad.
es.B: Yo le había hablado a él con orgullo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no me {{plural_you:han defraudado|habéis defraudado}}. Siempre {{plural_you:les|os}} hemos dicho la verdad, y del mismo modo lo que dijimos con orgullo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a Tito ha resultado ser verdad.
es.R: Yo le había dicho a Tito lo orgulloso que estaba de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y no me {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} quedar mal. Siempre {{plural_you:les|os}} hemos dicho la verdad. Y cuando le dijimos a Tito lo orgullosos que estábamos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, eso también resultó ser verdad.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa nimejivunia jambo lolote kwake kuhusu ninyi, sikuaibishwa; bali kama tulivyowaambia mambo yote kwa kweli, vivyo hivyo pia fahari yetu mbele ya Tito imethibitika kuwa kweli.
sw.B: Nilikuwa nimemweleza kwa fahari habari zenu, nanyi hamkuniangusha. Tumekuwa tukiwaambia kweli siku zote, na vivyo hivyo mambo tuliyomweleza Tito kwa fahari juu yenu yamethibitika kuwa kweli.
sw.R: Nilikuwa nimemwambia Tito jinsi ninavyoona fahari juu yenu, nanyi hamkunifanya nionekane mjinga. Tumewaambia kweli siku zote. Na tulipomwambia Tito jinsi tunavyoona fahari juu yenu, hilo pia limeonekana kuwa kweli.

decisions.choice: "if I have boasted anything": a modest way of saying "what I boasted"
decisions.reason: εἴ τι ("if anything") does not question that Paul spoke well of them; it plays down how much he had said. He had spoken of them to Titus before Titus set out.

decisions.choice: put to shame: shown up as wrong
decisions.reason: κατῃσχύνθην is to be disgraced when what one has trusted or claimed fails. The church's response proved Paul right.

decisions.choice: Paul's truthfulness toward them and toward Titus
alternatives: truth in the sense of the gospel
decisions.reason: The comparison links back to 1:15-24, where Paul defended himself against the charge of saying yes and no. What he says to them is true, and so was what he said about them.

decisions.choice: boasting: proper pride in the church
decisions.reason: καύχησις, like the verb earlier in the verse, is the good pride of verse 4 and 1:12-14.

decisions.choice: spoken proudly ... proud things we said (B); how proud I was (R)
decisions.reason: Following the book-wide choice on boasting, Literal keeps "boast" and the other levels speak of pride, since the argument here does not turn on the word itself.

decisions.choice: you did not let me down (B); you did not make me look foolish (R)
alternatives: I was not put to shame
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the church the subject, since its conduct is what kept Paul from being shamed (m2).

source.text: καὶ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐστιν ἀναμιμνῃσκομένου τὴν πάντων ὑμῶν ὑπακοήν, ὡς μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου ἐδέξασθε αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And the affections of him more abundantly toward you are, remembering the of all of you obedience, how with fear and trembling you received him.

en.L: And his tender affection is all the more toward you, as he remembers the obedience of all of you, how with fear and trembling you received him.
en.B: His deep love goes out to you all the more when he recalls how every one of you obeyed, and how you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
en.R: Titus loves you even more when he remembers how all of you were ready to obey. You welcomed him humbly and with deep respect, and you took his visit very seriously.

fr.L: Et sa tendre affection pour vous est d’autant plus grande qu’il se souvient de l’obéissance de vous tous, de la façon dont vous l’avez reçu avec crainte et tremblement.
fr.B: Il vous porte un amour profond, plus encore quand il se rappelle votre obéissance à tous, et comment vous l’avez accueilli avec crainte et tremblement.
fr.R: Tite vous aime encore plus quand il se souvient que vous étiez tous prêts à obéir. Vous l’avez accueilli humblement et avec un profond respect, et vous avez pris sa visite très au sérieux.

es.L: Y su entrañable afecto hacia {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es aún más abundante, al recordar la obediencia de todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, cómo lo {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} con temor y temblor.
es.B: Su profundo amor por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} crece aún más cuando recuerda cómo todos {{plural_you:ustedes obedecieron|vosotros obedecisteis}}, y cómo lo {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} con temor y temblor.
es.R: Tito {{plural_you:los|os}} ama todavía más cuando recuerda que todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:estaban|estabais}} dispuestos a obedecer. Lo {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} con humildad y profundo respeto, y {{plural_you:tomaron|tomasteis}} muy en serio su visita.

sw.L: Na upendo wake wa ndani kwenu unazidi zaidi, akikumbuka utii wenu nyote, jinsi mlivyompokea kwa hofu na kutetemeka.
sw.B: Upendo wake mkubwa unawaelekea zaidi anapokumbuka jinsi kila mmoja wenu alivyotii, na jinsi mlivyompokea kwa hofu na kutetemeka.
sw.R: Tito anawapenda hata zaidi anapokumbuka jinsi ninyi nyote mlivyokuwa tayari kutii. Mlimkaribisha kwa unyenyekevu na kwa heshima kubwa, na mliichukulia ziara yake kwa uzito mkubwa.

decisions.choice: deep affection, felt in the inner being
decisions.reason: σπλάγχνα literally means the inner organs, which Greek speakers treated as the seat of strong feeling, much as we speak of the heart (Philippians 1:8; 2:1).

decisions.choice: obedience: to the instructions of Paul's letter, received through Titus
decisions.reason: ὑπακοήν recalls 2:9, where Paul wrote to test whether they were obedient in everything. Titus saw that obedience at first hand.

decisions.choice: with fear and trembling: with humble, anxious respect, eager to do right
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of a serious, humble attitude before a task or a messenger (1 Corinthians 2:3; Philippians 2:12). The church took Titus's visit seriously; it was not afraid of him as a person.

decisions.choice: all the more: his affection has grown
decisions.reason: περισσοτέρως is comparative, as in 2:4: Titus's affection has grown because of what he saw.

decisions.choice: tender affection (L); deep love (B); loves (R)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:8, the levels give the sense of deep feeling rather than the image of the inner organs (m1).

decisions.choice: humbly and with deep respect ... took his visit very seriously
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase so that it does not sound as if the church was terrified (m3).

decisions.choice: entrañable afecto (L); profundo amor (B); ama (R)
decisions.reason: The Spanish word list gives "entrañas" at Literal for this word, but with "his ... toward you" it would read oddly in Spanish; "entrañable afecto" keeps the picture of the inner self, and Balanced and Readable follow the English.

decisions.choice: upendo wake wa ndani (L); upendo wake mkubwa (B)
decisions.reason: As in 6:12, the Greek word for the inner organs is the seat of affection; Swahili says "upendo wa ndani" (inner love) at Literal and "upendo mkubwa" (deep love) at Balanced.

source.text: χαίρω ὅτι ἐν παντὶ θαρρῶ ἐν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: I rejoice that in everything I am confident in you.

en.L: I rejoice that in everything I am confident in you.
en.B: I rejoice that in every way I can rely on you.
en.R: I am so glad that I can trust you completely.

fr.L: Je me réjouis de ce qu’en tout j’ai confiance en vous.
fr.B: Je me réjouis de pouvoir compter sur vous en toutes choses.
fr.R: Je suis très heureux de pouvoir vous faire entièrement confiance.

es.L: Me alegro de que en todo tengo confianza en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Me alegro de que en todo puedo contar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Estoy muy contento de que puedo confiar en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por completo.

sw.L: Nafurahi kwamba katika kila jambo nina uhakika nanyi.
sw.B: Nafurahi kwamba katika kila jambo ninaweza kuwategemea.
sw.R: Nafurahi sana kwamba ninaweza kuwaamini kabisa.

decisions.choice: confident about you: able to rely on you
decisions.reason: θαρρῶ means to be of good courage or confident. With ἐν ὑμῖν ("in you") it most likely means Paul can rely on them. It could also mean that they give him courage; both fit the joy of the verse.

decisions.choice: a closing sentence that prepares for chapters 8-9
decisions.reason: The verse closes the account that began at 2:12 and the defense of Paul's ministry since 1:12. Paul's confidence in them prepares for his appeal about the collection in chapters 8-9.

decisions.choice: rely on you (B); trust you completely (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for being confident in someone (m1).
